subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact five-headed hydra design in a dark, gritty God of War aesthetic—bronze and blood-red tones with scarred scales, a low quadruped body around 4m long and 1.6m high, with five necks fanning out into distinct horned heads.

I'm sketching the skeleton structure: a hip root, a spine chain, five neck chains of four joints each ending in jaw-equipped heads, plus IK legs and a tail chain, all while setting up a color palette of scale greens, bone whites, bronze, iron, and ember-red for the build.

Setting up the joint hierarchy...

Now I'm planning the body geometry: sweeping a tapered torso along the spine path with elliptical radii and a belly-colored sector, a tapering tail sweep, and a loop placing front/back legs mirrored left-right with shoulder and foot anchors feeding into limb IK.

I'm simplifying the leg chains to two segments each (hip-knee-foot), sweeping thick rounded tubes for limbs, and adding flattened box feet with claw spikes. Now I'm setting up the multi-neck layout with symmetric base offsets along the chest for the hydra heads.

For each neck, I'm computing a fan-out angle based on its index, then building a four-point curve from the chest base through control points that spread outward and upward to a head endpoint, with each neck's chain joints named sequentially and parented to the spine's tip joint.

Still defining head and jaw joints...

I'm adding battle damage details like scars, a broken spear embedded in one neck, and a shackled chain for dramatic flair, plus spine spikes and bone ridge plates. I'm setting up scale factors so the central head is larger than the others, then writing the head-building code with local offset functions for positioning parts like the skull frustum.

Writing head geometry code...

Still defining facial features...

I'm posing the jaws with varying open angles and adding a glowing ember in the central head's throat. I'll skip extra collar bands and just keep belly sectors on the neck, then adjust the tail to lie lower near the ground with a tapering curve down to a thin tip instead of floating.

Checking that feet and tail tips actually touch the floor at y=0, I'm sizing the foot spheres and verifying the leg bone lengths and hip joint placement reach correctly from the body down to the feet, then sweeping the body mesh along the spine chain.

Next I'm positioning the neck bases on the chest segment, making sure the starting path point sits inside the body radius so there's no gap, and working out per-neck x-offsets for the multi-head setup.

Each neck gets its own forward/upward spread based on its horizontal offset, with four control points curving from the chest up to a head position -- I'm shaping it as an S-curve so the head leans forward naturally rather than sticking straight up.

Now I'm sweeping the neck geometry with a tapering radius, adding bony spikes along the dorsal ridge spaced evenly, and starting to lay out similar spike rows along the back.

For the body I'm adding scale-plate ridges along the spine, shoulder spurs on the legs, and belly color sectors. For the feet I'm placing claw spikes angled outward from each toe tip, anchored to the last leg joint.

Tail spikes get added along a sweep with decreasing size toward the tip, and I'm deciding to skip war-paint details in favor of texture work later. I'm also planning naming conventions for each part—body, neck, skull, tail—and sketching the import statement and builder API usage for chains, limbs, and sweeps that will construct the creature.

Setting up quadruped leg positions with front and hind offsets, parenting legs and spine joints to the hips, and working out naming for texture requests like "body," "neck", and "tail" while being careful about duplicate names across repeated neck segments.

Now I'm adding glowing eye spheres, then moving on to write the actual construction code.
